summary: This note traces the city's local music scene decade by decade, from the 1970s rock and soul era through 1980s electronic music, 1990s DIY and crossover production, the 2000s digital shift, 2010s streaming and indie artists, and the 2020s vinyl revival. It names key local acts, their signature songs and release dates, plus festivals, venues and a forthcoming heritage museum. It frames the scene as a continuous flow of innovation and tradition.
one_line: A decade-by-decade history of the local music scene from the 1970s to the 2020s, highlighting notable acts, hits, venues and a new heritage museum.
key_facts: The Starliters, a rock and soul band fronted by Jimmy “The Voice” Martino with lead guitarist Rebecca "Bex" Sinclair, were a 1970s local favorite.
The Starliters' hit single “Groove On” was released on October 15, 1973.
The annual Summer Solstice Festival began in 1975 and helped launch young musicians such as percussionist Luis Fernandez.
In the 1980s synthesizers, drum machines and Moog synthesizers pushed the scene toward electronic experimentation.
The Glimmer Twins (Sarah Klein and David “DJ Dazzle” Anderton) released “Neon Nights” on July 17, 1982, which became the unofficial anthem of local night owls.
Pop Night Tuesdays at the Neon Club introduced fans to upcoming pop acts in the 1980s.
In the 1990s producer Tyler "Groovebox" Garrett combined traditional rock with hip-hop beats to create a crossover genre.
The band Overdrive Odyssey recorded and distributed music directly to fans in the 1990s, moving away from the record label model.
Echo Park, fronted by Ava Lane, used early online music platforms and broke out with “City Dusk” on September 14, 2005.
Tessellation Theory, a folktronica group, had a viral hit with “Waves of Us” on May 16, 2013, using looping and layering.
Vibrant Vinyl Nights, established September 2, 2023, features DJs spinning classic records and modern tracks pressed on vinyl, held at an old fusion bar that was a 70s rock hub.
The Local Music Heritage Museum, set to open in late 2023 and led by curator Emily Johnston, will offer interactive exhibits on the local scene.
